items.title: Fuel price caps: cap set on 29 Oct is in force; MF sets caps for 31 Oct–2 Nov at 14:00
items.title_cs: Stropy cen paliv: platí strop vyhlášený 29. 10.; MF ve 14:00 vyhlásí ceny na 31. 10.–2. 11.
items.note: Mechanism (MF press release 26 Oct): on every working day at 14:00, MF publishes maximum prices for the next day, and on non-working days the last announced price applies. Cap = 3-day rolling average of four wholesale references (ORLEN/Unipetrol, MOL, ČEPRO, Platts-based) + regulated margin CZK 2.50/l, incl. VAT, rounded down to whole haléř. This covers non-premium E10 petrol and B7 diesel. Fines are enforced by Specializovaný finanční úřad. Diesel excise is cut by CZK 1.939/l (2.35 incl. VAT) to 8.011 CZK/l. Cabinet (26 Oct) extended both measures to 30 Nov; the new price decree runs 1–30 Nov. Recent caps from Cenový věstník: 23 Oct petrol 44.94 / diesel 48.70; 24–26 Oct 44.55 / 48.69; 27 Oct 44.47 / 48.96; 28–29 Oct 44.45 / 49.46 (diesel +0.50). The 30 Oct cap is published Thu 29 Oct 14:00. On Fri 30 Oct 14:00 MF should, as on Fri 23 Oct (věstník 109 covered 24–26 Oct), publish one cap for Sat 31 Oct–Mon 2 Nov. That would be the first cap under the November decree. Diesel is drifting up (TTF gas at €100/MWh, Brent ~$114 per Patria ticker) and petrol is flat-to-down. Forecastable: will the diesel cap for 30 Oct exceed CZK 49.46? Will it stay above 49.00 for the weekend?

items.title: Coalition arithmetic after MP David Pražák quits ANO: coalition down to 107 of 200

items.note: Pražák, a third-term ANO MP, announced on 27 Oct that he is leaving ANO and will sit as an independent. He partly cited how the ČT/ČRo bill was handled ('partial, not fundamental'). He is due to become mayor of Semily. The coalition (ANO+SPD+Motoristé) won 108 seats, so it is now 107 plus an independent and keeps its majority. ANO club chair Malá called the move unfair. items.title: Unemployment-benefit cut and labour-code 'dependent work' redefinition before Social Committee; SPD opposes, unions campaign
items.title_cs: Snížení podpor v nezaměstnanosti a nová definice závislé práce v sociálním výboru; SPD proti, odbory v kampani
items.note: The Chamber passed the labour-code amendment in first reading on 20 Oct and sent it to the Social Committee (no committee date published). From January it would cut benefits in the first two months from 80% to 65% of earnings, with a cap of 60% of the average wage (CZK 28,903 instead of 38,537). Months 3–4 stay at 50%, then 45% instead of 40%. Requalification pay falls from 80% to 60%. Savings are put at ~CZK 5bn a year, and the 2027 budget already assumes ~4bn. SPD (Okamura: 'SPD pro to hlasovat nebude') opposes. ČT24 put ANO+Motoristé at 93 votes, now 92 after Pražák. An all-opposition amendment would keep current benefits. ČMKOS launched the 'Nechci IČO!' campaign (26 Oct) against the redefinition of dependent work. PAQ Research says it could legalise 70–90% of švarcsystém (50–80k people). Forecastable: will the benefit cut be dropped or softened in committee?
